title: Laredo recognizes November as Pancreatic Cancer Awareness Month
excerpt: Mayor Dr. Victor D. Treviño issued a proclamation recognizing November 2026 as Pancreatic Cancer Awareness Month in Laredo, urging early detection, education, and support for patients and families.
content:
Mayor Dr. Victor D. Treviño has issued an official proclamation recognizing November 2026 as Pancreatic Cancer Awareness Month in Laredo, according to the City of Laredo.

The proclamation highlights the importance of early detection, education, and support for people affected by the disease. Pancreatic cancer is the third leading cause of cancer-related deaths in the United States, the city said.

Recognizing warning signs — such as unexplained weight loss, back pain, and jaundice — can help people seek medical attention sooner, according to the city.

During the ceremony, the names of local people who lost their lives to cancer were read aloud in a tribute honoring their memories and their families.

Mayor Treviño also emphasized the importance of improving access to cancer care closer to home and supporting patients and caregivers throughout their journey.

Residents are encouraged to wear purple this November, spread awareness, and stand with those affected by pancreatic cancer. More information is available at cancer.org.

Source: City of Laredo - Government (Facebook), Nov. 12, 2026.
